skills.name: Non-renewable energy sources and their uses

note.text:
An energy source is something from which we get energy. A non-renewable source is used up faster than nature can replace it: one day it will run out.
Non-renewable sources:
• fossil fuels, formed over millions of years from dead plants and animals: coal, crude oil (giving petrol, diesel, kerosene) and natural gas (cooking gas);
• nuclear fuel: uranium.
Uses: petrol and diesel for cars, buses and generators; kerosene for lamps and stoves; cooking gas; thermal power stations that make electricity; Cameroon exports crude oil.
Problems: they will run out; burning them gives smoke and carbon dioxide, which pollute the air and warm the Earth; oil spills harm the sea.
Renewable sources (sun, wind, flowing water as at the Edéa and Song Loulou dams, trees that are replanted) do not run out.

worked_example.problem: A family uses {f} when there is no electricity. Name its energy source, say if it is renewable, and give one problem.
steps: Petrol comes from crude oil, a fossil fuel.
Fossil fuels are non-renewable: they will run out.
Burning petrol gives smoke and carbon dioxide, which pollute the air.
worked_example.answer: Crude oil (petrol), non-renewable; it pollutes the air.

example: Renewable sources, like the sun, do not run out.

pick.q: Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?
pick.r: They will run out: they form far more slowly than we use them.
w: They come from the sun every day.
pick.y: We use them much faster than they form.

pick.q: Which is a problem of burning fossil fuels?
pick.r: It pollutes the air with smoke and carbon dioxide.
pick.y: Burning releases smoke and carbon dioxide.

pick.q: Which source of electricity in Cameroon is renewable?

w: a thermal power station burning oil
pick.y: Flowing water does not run out.
